versions.changelog:
Pass user-controlled text to workflow scripts via env, not interpolation

The develop publish run failed with:

  /home/runner/work/_temp/....sh: line 18: syntax error near unexpected
  token `('

Actions substitutes a ${{ }} expression into the script text before bash
parses it, so the commit message in

  CHANGELOG=$(printf '%s' "${{ github.event.head_commit.message }}" | ...)

was pasted in verbatim. A message containing a quote and a parenthesis --
here a line reading: Register "(^|/)index\.html$" instead -- closes the
string early and leaves bash parsing the rest as code.

That is also a command injection vector, not just a syntax hazard: this
workflow runs with contents: write and pushes to main, and the message is
attacker-supplied on any branch that triggers a publish. Same for the
release body and tag name, which feed the release manifest job. Git refs
permit '(', ';' and '&', so a crafted tag reaches the same place.

Pass all of these through env: instead. The runner sets those as
environment data, so the value never becomes part of the script.

Covered every user-controlled expression used inside a run: block, not
only the one that failed -- the release path has the identical defect and
would have broken the next release. The tag validation in the release
manifest job now actually protects something: previously a malformed tag
broke the script before the regex check could reject it.
